title: Dedicated customer-instance hosting for explorEDA
mode: Research and architecture shaping only; no implementation or provisioning

decision.fallback_scope: Simpler always-on application operation, conditional on two-provider state provisioning and container-level isolation being acceptable.
decision.challenger_test_trigger: A mandatory primary gate fails, or measured cost/operational requirements make a challenger materially preferable.

primary_configuration.runtime: trusted Linux amd64 OCI image, one release digest for all customers
primary_configuration.health: HTTP/1 liveness on 8081 in same application process; only 8080 exposed in container ports
primary_configuration.production_smoke_routing: Reserved ALB path and serverless NEG mask selecting service and tag; narrow application authorization for exact customer/generation; remove tag after proof
primary_configuration.image_portability: The common image must support configurable provider-compatible HTTP/1 API or h2c ingress; proxy and cancellation behavior require a separate proof per host

assumptions: No provider account, region, database engine, contractual isolation or availability tier, budget or fleet count selected by user; values are scenarios.
Trusted application code; no arbitrary customer native code or unrestricted shell/UDF execution.
Public TLS database access is acceptable in the default network profile; static/private routes are separately qualified.
No production SLA is inferred from provider documentation or paid-customer status.
Instance-based min-zero billing is a conservative health-compatible default; request billing is only an optimization sensitivity.
Pricing credits and free allowances shared once per relevant account/project, not multiplied per customer.

recommendations.proposal: Use one Cloud Run Gen2 service per customer as the default hosting architecture.
recommendations.rationale: It combines ordinary native-driver containers, per-service identity and lifecycle, microVM isolation, regional placement, documented networking and request-driven scale-to-zero. The future backend is new work; current static hosting is not that backend.
recommendations.benefit: Dedicated customer query runtime without a guest OS fleet.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Maintain one image, app health/auth/query safety, bounded provisioning code and a small shared Google control plane.
recommendations.alternative: Render always-on service/customer; Cloudflare Containers can displace the winner if its proof passes.

recommendations.proposal: Define the customer instance as an independently deployed service plus its exclusive replicas, identity, credentials and state resources.
recommendations.rationale: A service can scale from zero to several customer-exclusive microVMs. It is not a dedicated physical host or customer cloud account. A database/schema alone does not isolate query compute.
recommendations.benefit: An honest dedicated-instance promise and smaller compromise boundary.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Per-customer service, IAM and object/secret resource inventory; shared regional/account risks remain.
recommendations.alternative: Separate project/account for administrative, quota, contractual or network requirements.

recommendations.proposal: Start at 1 vCPU/2 GiB, instance-based billing, automatic min zero, service-level max two, h2c ingress and separate HTTP/1 application liveness.
recommendations.rationale: Conservative billing avoids ambiguity in current health-probe documentation and permits recovery/cleanup outside requests. Idle tails must be measured; max two is not a hard cap.
recommendations.benefit: Provider-driven hang recovery with scale-to-zero and a credible cost model.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Two listeners in one application; health must reflect event-loop readiness, and billing/scale-down must be proved.
recommendations.alternative: Request-based billing after health/billing proof; min-one configuration for customers who pay for warm readiness.

recommendations.proposal: Connect to customer-owned databases using verified TLS and a narrowly privileged read-only identity by default.
recommendations.rationale: Hosting a new customer database adds backup, migration, upgrade and billing commitments that the user has not selected.
recommendations.benefit: Keeps initial product responsibility bounded and preserves the customer source of truth.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Customer onboarding still needs database credentials, permitted objects, region and network path; connection/timeout behavior is adapter-specific.
recommendations.alternative: A separately priced managed database/customer if the product must ingest and own customer data.

recommendations.proposal: Push supported relational work to the source database and stream bounded results; do not transmit the complete internal AnalysisEvaluation by default.
recommendations.rationale: Current evaluations include full stage rows and contributor arrays, and consumers create additional row copies. Naive serialization can erase database pushdown savings.
recommendations.benefit: Bounds server memory, browser memory and billed bytes while preserving complete snapshots when feasible.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Reconcile query demand, provenance and scalar semantics with unfinished tracks; add explicit incomplete/error semantics.
recommendations.alternative: Bounded local evaluation in the customer container when pushdown cannot preserve semantics.

recommendations.proposal: Keep admitted full snapshots in the browser and make server caches disposable and disabled initially.
recommendations.rationale: The notebook intent does not imply server DuckDB or permanent cache. Durable caching introduces freshness, permission and invalidation work.
recommendations.benefit: Fast local interaction after loading with fewer server lifecycle dependencies.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Enforce byte/row budgets and move decoding/indexing work off the main thread; local data already delivered cannot be remotely recalled.
recommendations.alternative: Tenant-scoped immutable snapshot objects only after repeated-transfer measurements justify them.

recommendations.proposal: Require end-to-end cancellation proof, database statement deadlines and independent cancellation capacity.
recommendations.rationale: Cloud Run HTTP/1 disconnects are not propagated; staleness suppression is not cancellation. A separate cancel request can reach a different replica or revision.
recommendations.benefit: Avoids runaway SQL, exhausted pools and misleading canceled UI states.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Actual driver must cancel owned work, reserve any control connection and close transactions/cursors; h2c must survive ingress.
recommendations.alternative: Same-connection WebSocket control or tenant-scoped owner dispatch only if the simpler HTTP/2 path fails.

recommendations.proposal: Give each runtime only its own secret and object permissions, and validate browser identity against the fixed customer identity.
recommendations.rationale: Hostname routing, a shared login provider and a service account solve different problems. Fleet control-plane database access would unnecessarily broaden runtime authority.
recommendations.benefit: Limits accidental routing mistakes and a customer-runtime compromise.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Maintain narrow bindings, host-bound sessions, per-customer authorization and credential rotation.
recommendations.alternative: Customer-owned project/account when separate administrators or keys are required.

recommendations.proposal: Use one small shared desired-state reconciler with one durable record per customer.
recommendations.rationale: Deterministic resource names, operation IDs, leases and observed readiness are enough for this finite lifecycle; payment and workflow platforms are unnecessary initially.
recommendations.benefit: Repeatable provisioning, retry and retirement without manual fleet administration.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: A Cloud Run controller job, Firestore control records and one regional reconciliation schedule; immediate commands use the same path.
recommendations.alternative: Private versioned manifests plus the same small CI/API script when initial onboarding is operator-triggered.

recommendations.proposal: Build one digest per release and deploy whole-customer cohorts with explicit rollback and tag cleanup.
recommendations.rationale: Customer code forks and long intra-service traffic splits multiply states and pools. Old revisions, retained tags and deploy overrides have provider-specific lifecycle effects.
recommendations.benefit: A manageable release surface and a recoverable bad-deploy path.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Retain old images; keep storage formats backward compatible; reconcile desired and observed digest; route production tagged smoke tests through a reserved ALB service/tag mask with application authorization; remove smoke tags.
recommendations.alternative: A warm fixed service plus a simple CI deploy command for the first few customers.

recommendations.proposal: Externalize project/configuration state in a bucket/customer with versioning, explicit retention and restore proof.
recommendations.rationale: Runtime files disappear on restart; object-backed file mounts do not provide the locking semantics of a normal database filesystem.
recommendations.benefit: Rebuildable customer instances and portable exports.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Object generation checks, retention accounting, backup/restore exercise and separate secret recovery.
recommendations.alternative: S3 via exact-service Render OIDC for fallback; managed database only when transactional shared state becomes a real requirement.

recommendations.proposal: Treat public TLS, shared static egress, customer-exclusive egress and private/on-premises access as separate network profiles.
recommendations.rationale: Direct VPC/NAT can add severe cold readiness latency; shared IP is not customer-specific identity; private access always requires a supported customer-side path.
recommendations.benefit: Avoids selling networking that the chosen provider does not actually supply.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Preflight each database path; price shared infrastructure once and customer-dedicated paths separately.
recommendations.alternative: Fly app/customer for cheap static egress; dedicated cloud project/VPC or customer connector when necessary.

recommendations.proposal: Use a paid Render 1c-2g service/customer as the simpler always-on fallback.
recommendations.rationale: Render supplies managed TLS, health restart and deployment handling. One Pro workspace plus an isolated environment/customer preserves separate application runtimes.
recommendations.benefit: Simpler continuous application operation and predictable compute floor.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: External S3 state adds AWS OIDC/IAM/bucket setup; this is not universally simpler end to end. Initial 100-service creation is throttled across several hours.
recommendations.alternative: Keep Cloud Run and use min one if cold starts alone are the problem; Fly if a guest-kernel or cheap unique-egress requirement dominates.

recommendations.proposal: Give Cloudflare Containers a bounded challenger proof using the default scheduler and one Worker/application/customer.
recommendations.rationale: Current Firecracker isolation, native containers and actual-CPU/low-egress pricing are relevant. Exact database placement, native TCP fixed egress, cancellation and multi-resource rollout need proof.
recommendations.benefit: Can reduce recurring transfer and I/O-heavy compute cost without a guest OS fleet.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Worker/DO/container lifecycle and separate image readiness; do not rely on beta snapshots or per-instance scheduler.
recommendations.alternative: Cloud Run baseline with documented regional network options.

recommendations.proposal: Keep pure Workers as a constrained database-streaming specialization, not the general default.
recommendations.rationale: Streaming may fit within 128 MB even when total output exceeds that size; ordinary native addons and broad local analytical work do not. Hyperdrive adds engine, pool and configuration limits.
recommendations.benefit: Potentially very low idle/transfer costs for bounded adapters.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Maintain Worker-compatible driver/encoder path and prove Hyperdrive transaction/cancellation/cache semantics; request quota increase beyond 25 configs.
recommendations.alternative: Ordinary OCI container/customer.

recommendations.proposal: Do not use a VPS fleet or shared-host customer containers as the default for this maintenance objective.
recommendations.rationale: VM creation is automatable but guest patching, restart coordination, capacity and restore remain operator work; shared hosts also share a kernel and outage domain.
recommendations.benefit: Avoids turning one developer into a small infrastructure operator.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: A VPS remains an exception with an explicit operating budget and rebuild/restore procedure.
recommendations.alternative: Managed customer-specific services or tasks.

recommendations.proposal: Defer ECS Express/Fargate unless AWS locality or consistently occupied instances changes the economics.
recommendations.rationale: Express now automates much AWS setup, but the default retains one task/customer and load-balancer/IP floors; minimum zero does not supply request-driven wake.
recommendations.benefit: A credible AWS-native route without Kubernetes.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Task roles/security groups, ALB groups, networking and AWS billing dimensions remain; exact Virginia internet DTO quote is still open.
recommendations.alternative: Cloud Run for sleeping customers or Render for simple always-on operations.

recommendations.proposal: Reject a shared multi-customer query process and Kubernetes/custom fleet orchestration for the baseline.
recommendations.rationale: A shared query process changes the requested dedicated runtime; a custom scheduler adds work without solving a demonstrated missing requirement.
recommendations.benefit: Preserves product intent and keeps the architecture runnable by one developer.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: One provider-specific provisioning adapter is still necessary; avoid attempting provider-neutral infrastructure abstractions.
recommendations.alternative: Shared ingress, auth and provisioning only; independent customer query services.

recommendations.proposal: Complete local contract proof and then a separately authorized two-customer hosted sandbox before commitment.
recommendations.rationale: Documents and mocks cannot establish proxy behavior, driver cancellation, memory, cold starts, identity bindings or actual bills.
recommendations.benefit: Can reject the architecture before a production fleet or product promise is created.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: A short-lived synthetic test, measured checklist and complete cleanup; do not execute during this research assignment.
recommendations.alternative: No production launch until failed gates are fixed, scoped out with a product decision or select a different host.

recommendations.proposal: Defer hosted source databases, permanent embedded databases, cross-region HA and private customer connectors from the first baseline.
recommendations.rationale: These introduce durable-state, consistency, network and service-level commitments that have not been selected and are not forced by the row range.
recommendations.benefit: Keeps provisioning and operation bounded while preserving explicit migration paths.
recommendations.maintenance_cost: Revisit each capability with workload evidence and separately priced ownership/support obligations.
recommendations.alternative: Customer-owned database and external project state; short-lived embedded scratch only.

proof_gates.name: Local contract and driver proof
proof_gates.pass: Two separate local processes or containers using the same image, each with one fixed customer identity, plus real local database drivers, 10k/100k narrow fixtures and wide/large sensitivities preserve scalar, filter, identity and provenance semantics; bounded snapshot or explicit too-large result.
proof_gates.reject: Current full-stage serialization or driver buffering is unavoidable within selected memory; query/transport tracks cannot reconcile semantics.

proof_gates.name: Isolation
proof_gates.pass: Cross-customer token/hostname/query-ID, secret, object and network attempts fail; A saturation does not consume B query slots or B data credentials.
proof_gates.reject: Any cross-customer data/authority leak or misrepresented runtime boundary.

proof_gates.name: Cancellation and health
proof_gates.pass: Confirmed native SQL cancellation within proposed 2 seconds for explicit cancel/disconnect; every SQL operation has a bounded DB deadline; crash and hung application recover without operator intervention.
proof_gates.reject: Cancel can only stop browser rendering, waits behind exhausted pool, reaches wrong owner, or health conceals a hung app.

proof_gates.name: Streaming and responsiveness
proof_gates.pass: First batch arrives before full result; slow-reader backpressure keeps primary RSS below 1.5 GiB on its 2 GiB plan. Cloudflare Containers proves headroom on its actual 3 GiB shape; pure Workers proves peak isolate memory comfortably below 128 MB including WASM, virtual filesystem, buffers and concurrent invocations. Completed snapshot is verified by final marker/count/checksum; browser remains interactive under explicit frame/long-task targets.
proof_gates.reject: Unbounded buffers, silent partial success, main-thread stalls, or memory growth proportional to all stage rows/contributors.

proof_gates.name: Provision/update/recovery
proof_gates.pass: Duplicate and interrupted creates converge to one owned service; proposed ready-without-DNS budget of 10 minutes; bad deploy rolls back within 5 minutes; old/new streams close correctly; drift reconciles and tags removed.
proof_gates.reject: Unrecoverable manual resource repair, leaked duplicate resources, lost state, or mixed image/config promoted as ready.

proof_gates.name: Networking and cold readiness
proof_gates.pass: Chosen DB route verifies TLS and required egress identity; proposed public-path p95 cold-to-first-result target of 5 seconds for a fast fixture; mandatory static/private route passes separately or an explicit warm tier is selected.
proof_gates.reject: Undocumented required fixed TCP egress, unacceptable region/residency, or private/cold path fails agreed product SLO.

proof_gates.name: Suspend/revoke/resume
proof_gates.pass: Immediate controller command removes smoke tags and disables new service admission; bounded in-flight SQL drains/cancels; resume restores exact healthy spec; user revocation follows a declared and tested token/session expiry policy.
proof_gates.reject: Tagged endpoints bypass suspension, stale authorization remains beyond declared window, or shared resources deleted.

proof_gates.name: Costs and scale-to-zero
proof_gates.pass: Measured awake time, CPU, compressed/uncompressed bytes and billing SKUs explain the modeled bill; no unbounded admission or egress; dormant service actually sleeps with health configured.
proof_gates.reject: Invoice diverges by more than proposed 20 percent after unit/allowance normalization, idle tails prevent viable pricing, or required networking adds an unaccepted floor.

proof_gates.name: Export/restore/retire
proof_gates.pass: Fresh replacement service restores acknowledged projects/config under proposed 30 minute RTO; versioned acknowledged save recovered, source DB untouched, credentials reissued, one customer deletion cannot affect another.
proof_gates.reject: Local disk was authoritative, retention/old versions missing, exported data incomplete without warning, or broad deletion touches shared/customer-owned resources.

regions.cloud_run: us-central1 with North America public recipients
regions.aws: us-east-1 unless a source is explicitly described otherwise

assumptions: Requests are sequential in wall-time arithmetic; actual CPU utilization of 25 percent when bursty or 50 percent when steady is not measured throughput.
22 awake instance-hours includes all idle tails and is independent of request count; isolated requests can produce much larger tails.
Cloudflare custom shape of 1 vCPU, 3 GiB memory and 4 GB disk; pure Workers with 128 MB memory is not performance-equivalent.
Render and Cloudflare decimal egress interpretation is an explicit planning assumption where docs label GB/TB without a byte definition; reconcile actual meter.
Base state model: 2 GiB retained/customer, 1,000 writes and 100,000 reads monthly, 2 active secret versions for primary.
Primary operational allowance: 3 USD/fleet/month for bounded controller/build/registry/DNS work, not a fixed vendor fee.
No trial credits, taxes, negotiated discounts, production source DB charges, private networking, premium support or unmeasured deployment/startup overhead included in core tables.

cost_model.aws_internet_transfer_rate_gap: The public EC2 page confirmed 100 GB shared free DTO, but the current Virginia per-GB table and price API could not be retrieved. ECS values are explicitly stable floors plus LCU and transfer; no Ireland rate is substituted.

handoffs.query_demand: Bound row/decoded-byte/compute/duration budgets; preserve provenance/filter semantics; separate request ID from snapshot identity; define cancel, stale and incomplete states.
handoffs.transport: Incremental decoder and bounded batches/backpressure; complete snapshot marker and count/checksum; type preservation; avoid automatic full-stage/contributor arrays; off-main-thread client work.
handoffs.database_adapters: Container-compatible real drivers with TLS, streaming/cursors, native cancellation and narrow read-only credentials; explicit pooling/private-network/static-egress/capability limits.

unresolved_choices: What does dedicated mean contractually: separate application runtime, guest kernel, exclusive egress, or customer-owned cloud account?
Which database engines/locations must launch support, and are public TLS/shared allowlisted IPs acceptable?
What cold-start and availability expectations, usage shape and target customer-level cost justify min-zero versus warm/always-on operation?

production: Unfinished companion query/transport/adapter contracts must reconcile.
Chosen database driver/network, customer isolation wording and cold/availability targets remain provisional.
Hosted proofs have not been executed or authorized by this research assignment.
evidence_gaps: Render guest-kernel guarantee and HTTP abort propagation not established.
Cloudflare dedicated native TCP egress, exact database placement/SLA and HTTP-to-driver cancellation not established.
Current Virginia AWS internet DTO rate not retrieved.

sources.title: Cloud Run security
claims: Container-instance isolation uses a VMM; Gen2 provides a dedicated microVM boundary.
Containers in one instance share that instance boundary.

sources.title: Cloud Run execution environments
claims: Gen2 provides full Linux compatibility and supports native container workloads.
Environment choice affects startup and resource requirements.

sources.title: Cloud Run quotas and limits
claims: 1,000 services/project/region; control-plane read 3,000/minute and write 180/minute/project/region.
32 MiB HTTP/1 request and buffered response limits; streamed/chunked response exemption and HTTP/2 request distinction.
Maximum request timeout 60 minutes; max concurrency 1,000; max 8 vCPU and 32 GiB.
Regional CPU/memory/Direct VPC capacity must be checked; new Instance resource is distinct from service replicas.

sources.title: Cloud Run pricing
claims: us-central1 Tier 1 request active CPU $0.000024/vCPU-s, memory $0.0000025/GiB-s, requests $0.40/million.
Idle minimum instance CPU/memory $0.0000025 per relevant second; instance billing CPU $0.000018/vCPU-s and memory $0.000002/GiB-s.
Free allowances aggregate across projects on a billing account.
Ephemeral disk price $0.000109589/GiB-hour.

sources.title: Cloud Run maximum instances
claims: Service-level and revision-level maximums differ.
Tagged revisions excluded from traffic split are not covered by service-level maximum in the same way.
Maximum settings are not strict guarantees against temporary overshoot.

sources.title: Cloud Run instance autoscaling
claims: Temporary maximum-instance overshoot can occur on maintenance and traffic spikes; excess can exceed twice the setting.
Old/new revisions can overlap; idle instances can be retained.
Pending requests queue for a bounded interval.

sources.title: Mapping custom domains
claims: Native mapping remains Preview, not production-ready because of latency.
No wildcard certificate support; regional limitations.
External Application Load Balancer is the recommended production approach.

sources.title: Configure request timeout
claims: Default 300 seconds, maximum 3,600.
504 does not stop container processing.
Long requests need reconnect/idempotency handling.

sources.title: Cloud Run container runtime contract
claims: Writable default filesystem is in memory, counts against RAM, and is nonpersistent.
CPU allocation and shutdown behavior constrain background work.
Container HTTP/2 requires cleartext h2c while platform terminates TLS.

sources.title: Configure service identity
claims: Attach a runtime service account and grant only required access.
Runtime identity and deployer identity are separate.

sources.title: Configure secrets
claims: Runtime service identity needs secret access.
Pin environment secret versions; mounted secrets fetch versions at read time.

sources.title: Static outbound IP address
claims: Static outbound address requires routing through VPC and Cloud NAT with reserved addresses.
All-traffic routing is required for the documented public static egress path.

sources.title: Direct VPC egress
claims: Startup network establishment can take a minute or more.
With Cloud NAT, cold starts may have delays of 30 seconds or more; connector suggested for better startup performance.
Direct VPC uses network tags and can retain allocated addresses beyond shutdown.

sources.title: Cloud NAT pricing
claims: Public NAT $0.0014 per assigned VM-hour capped at $0.044/hour beyond 32.
External address $0.005/hour.
Data processed $0.045/GiB in each direction; actual Cloud Run assignment count requires validation.

sources.title: VPC network pricing
claims: Serverless VPC Access connector VMs incur Compute Engine prices.
Networking and NAT charges remain separate.

sources.title: Cloud Load Balancing pricing
claims: First five global forwarding rules $0.025/hour total.
Application load balancer data processing $0.008/GiB in and out, plus relevant transfer.
Topology-specific rules apply; avoid duplicate transfer charging.

sources.title: Global external Application Load Balancer with serverless backend
claims: Serverless NEG URL masks support extracting service from hostname or path.
Regional backend selection requires deliberate configuration.

sources.title: Configure ephemeral disk volumes
claims: Preview; Gen2 only; per-volume 1–100 GiB, up to ten volumes.
Default per-instance disk quota 10 GiB; first deployment can automatically grant 100 GiB regional quota.
Disk does not persist across instance replacement; max-instance allocation interacts with regional quota.

sources.title: Rollouts, rollbacks, and traffic migration
claims: Immutable revisions support no-traffic deployment, controlled traffic migration, and rollback.

sources.title: Manually scale services
claims: Manual scaling to zero disables a service.
Returning to automatic scaling restores normal request-driven behavior.

sources.title: Cloud Run billing settings
claims: Request-based versus instance-based CPU allocation.
Cloud Run budget spend caps are Preview.
Contains health-probe billing guidance that should be reconciled with detailed health-check documentation in proof.

sources.title: Budget spend caps
claims: Preview caps apply to one supported product in one project, not per Cloud Run customer service.
Enforcement and recovery can lag; overages remain billable; fixed costs can continue.

sources.title: Cloud Run troubleshooting: client disconnect
claims: HTTP/1.1 client disconnect events are not propagated to the container.
Use HTTP/2 or WebSockets for client-disconnect propagation.

sources.title: Use HTTP/2
claims: End-to-end HTTP/2 requires explicit configuration and h2c support.
Default Cloud Run forwarding can downgrade to HTTP/1.

sources.title: Cloud Run v2 services API
claims: API exposes desired/observed generations, etag, reconciling status, conditions and latest ready revision.
Supports durable lifecycle reconciliation.

sources.title: IAM quotas and limits
claims: Service-account count and CreateServiceAccount quotas vary by project.
Do not assume legacy universal quota 100.

sources.title: Serverless VPC Access
claims: Connectors have at least two VMs, maximum settings up to ten.
Connectors scale out, not back in automatically.

sources.title: Configure Serverless VPC Access connectors
claims: Smaller connector after scale-out requires recreation or replacement.
Connector compute floor and lifecycle differ from Direct VPC.

sources.title: General-purpose Compute Engine pricing
claims: Official search-indexed US Iowa e2-micro list rate $0.008376428/hour and f1-micro $0.0076/hour.
Full page open timed out; exact current rates were verified through official-domain search results, not a deployed billing estimate.

sources.title: Cloud NAT product interactions
claims: Direct VPC Cloud Run public NAT requires all-traffic routing.
Port allocation requires twice the ports needed per Cloud Run instance.

sources.title: Cloud Run health checks
claims: HTTP probes require an HTTP/1 endpoint; gRPC and TCP options differ.
CPU/memory used for probes are billed; verify billing-mode interaction.

sources.title: Configure CPU
claims: Fractional CPU requires Gen1, concurrency one, and request billing.
Startup CPU boost adds billed resources; baseline costs exclude it.

sources.title: Configure memory limits
claims: Gen2 minimum 512 MiB; 1 vCPU supports up to 4 GiB.
Memory sizing must account for per-request usage times concurrency.

sources.title: Lambda response streaming
claims: Synchronous streamed responses up to 200 MB; first 6 MB uncapped, then 2 MB/s.
Client disconnect does not halt a streaming invocation and full duration is billed.
Node.js/custom runtime support; VPC function URL streaming limitation and SDK streaming alternative.

sources.title: Lambda quotas
claims: Normal synchronous functions: 15 minutes, 128–10,240 MB memory, 512–10,240 MB tmp; CPU equivalent one vCPU at 1,769 MB.
Default concurrency 1,000; most control APIs share 15 requests/second.
MicroVMs ARM64-only; 8-hour max lifetime; hard 8 concurrent connections at 1 vCPU.
New accounts can have lower effective quotas.

sources.title: AWS Fargate pricing
claims: Virginia Linux x86 CPU $0.000011244/vCPU-s, memory $0.000001235/GB-s.
Virginia Linux ARM CPU $0.0000089944/vCPU-s, memory $0.0000009889/GB-s.
Billing starts with image download and has one-minute minimum for Linux.

sources.title: AWS Fargate for ECS
claims: Fargate task has hardware virtualization isolation and does not share kernel, CPU, memory or ENI with another task.
Containers within one task share its boundary.

sources.title: ECS Express Mode overview
claims: Managed workflow provisions Fargate, ALB HTTPS, monitoring, security groups and scaling.
No extra Express fee; underlying resources are billed.

sources.title: How ECS Express Mode works
claims: Defaults 1 vCPU/2 GiB, minimum one task, maximum twenty, CPU target 60%, canary deployment.
ALBs shared by up to 25 Express services in one VPC.
Deployment overlap temporarily adds resources; steady minimum is not inherently two tasks.

sources.title: Announcing ECS Express Mode
claims: November 2025 launch; available in all regions supporting ECS Fargate; no additional charge.

sources.title: ECS Express Mode ARM architecture support
claims: September 2026 official announcement of ARM architecture support.

sources.title: ECS service auto scaling
claims: Minimum capacity zero is possible.
Scaling from zero requires metric data; no automatic HTTP request buffering/wake is established by this feature.

sources.title: App Runner CreateService API
claims: App Runner stopped accepting new customers March 31, 2026; existing customers continue.

sources.title: Elastic Load Balancing pricing
claims: US East ALB $0.0225/hour plus $0.008/LCU-hour.
LCU dimensions include processed bytes, connections and rule evaluations.
Ordinary instance/IP target bytes dimension uses 1 GB/hour per LCU.

sources.title: Amazon VPC pricing
claims: Public IPv4 $0.005/hour per address.
Official Ohio NAT example $0.045/hour plus $0.045/GB; not used as a falsely verified Virginia quote.
NAT and ordinary transfer charges can coexist.

sources.title: Create a Lambda function from a container image
claims: Lambda image must implement Runtime API; read-only root filesystem with writable tmp.
A generic long-lived HTTP OCI image is not a drop-in function deployment.

sources.title: Lambda tenant isolation
claims: Tenant ID selects environments never reused across tenants, using Firecracker isolation.
All tenants share execution-role permissions; function URLs, provisioned concurrency and SnapStart unsupported.
Additional environment creation charges.

sources.title: Lambda Managed Instances
claims: Functions run on EC2 capacity providers operated by AWS.
Capacity provider is security boundary; per-function containers can share the host.

sources.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs
claims: Full OS, Firecracker isolation, dedicated HTTPS endpoints, HTTP2/gRPC/WebSockets, and automatic suspend/resume.
Distinct product from ordinary Lambda functions.

sources.title: Running and using Lambda MicroVMs
claims: Total running plus suspended lifespan 1–28,800 seconds; terminated afterward.
Each MicroVM has its own endpoint with mandatory JWE authentication; no shared load balancing.
Suspend/resume hooks must close/reopen connections and refresh credentials.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers limits
claims: Paid: 128 MB per isolate (shared by concurrent invocations), 30s default/300s configurable CPU; no enforced HTTP response body or connected HTTP wall-time cap. 64 MiB uncompressed bundle; 500 scripts/account; 100 custom domains/zone; 10,000 default paid subrequests adjustable to 10M; six initial outgoing connections.

sources.title: How Workers works
claims: V8 isolates separate memory within a shared runtime; isolates can be evicted and requests can reach different instances. This does not reserve a core, process or physical host for a customer.

sources.title: Cloudflare Workers pricing
claims: USD $5/account/month; 10M requests, 30M CPU-ms included; overages $0.30/M requests and $0.02/M CPU-ms; no Worker egress charge. Current logs 20M events included then $0.60/M, seven-day retention; pricing changes December 1, 2026.

sources.title: Workers for Platforms pricing
claims: $25 monthly, 20M requests, 60M CPU-ms and 1,000 scripts included; $0.30/M requests, $0.02/M CPU-ms, $0.02/additional script. Page still lists 30s CPU max/invocation; do not silently substitute normal Workers 300s limit.

sources.title: Workers for Platforms limits
claims: Unlimited scripts and Durable Object namespaces; user Workers lack gradual deployments and deploy all traffic at once. Shared API rate limit 1,200 requests/5min per user/account token.

sources.title: Workers for Platforms custom limits
claims: Dispatch can enforce per-invocation CPU and subrequest caps; a hit throws immediately.

sources.title: How Workers for Platforms works
claims: A dynamic dispatch Worker performs routing/authentication and invokes customer user Workers through namespace bindings; user Workers have separate resource bindings. Optional outbound Worker controls fetch requests.

sources.title: Hyperdrive limits
claims: Paid 25 configured databases/account; 60s statement timeout; responses above 50MB bypass cache but are still returned. Initial connect15s; idle10min; about100 origin connections/config as soft distributed limit. Limit increase requires approval and not all limits increase.

sources.title: Hyperdrive supported databases and features
claims: PostgreSQL9–18 and MySQL5.7–8 plus MariaDB supported; SQL Server/MongoDB unsupported. TLS required; verify-full mode supported. SQL-level prepared-statement management, advisory locks, LISTEN/NOTIFY and arbitrary per-session state unsupported.

sources.title: Hyperdrive connection pooling
claims: Transaction pooling; SET state resets when connection returns to pool. Minimum pool5, configurable soft max. Driver named prepared statements supported in postgres.js and node-postgres; manual restart can interrupt queries.

sources.title: Hyperdrive firewall and networking
claims: Origin firewall can allow Cloudflare IP ranges or use Tunnel. This is a shared Cloudflare-range allowlist, not a dedicated per-customer static egress address.

sources.title: Hyperdrive private database via Workers VPC
claims: Workers VPC TCP service routes Hyperdrive through cloudflared running inside a reachable private network; no Access application/service token required. Guide and sidebar mark beta; TLS defaults differ from newer supported-features page, so configure verification explicitly.

sources.title: Hyperdrive query caching
claims: Defaults max_age60s plus stale_while_revalidate15s; writes do not invalidate cached reads. Caching-disabled config retains pooling. Multiple configs for same database add to origin connection usage.

sources.title: Workers TCP sockets
claims: Outbound TCP supported; sockets must be created within a handler and cannot be shared from global scope. Direct connect to private/localhost/Cloudflare ranges is disallowed; no inbound TCP server.

sources.title: Workers Node.js compatibility
claims: Workers supports many Node APIs including stream/net/fs/zlib; some modules are partial implementations or nonfunctional stubs. It is not a general Node/Linux runtime.

sources.title: Workers fs
claims: Memory-based virtual filesystem includes read-only bundle and writable temporary files; temporary contents count against Worker memory. It is not a persistent disk or free spill space.

sources.title: Workers placement
claims: Explicit cloud-region hints place near AWS/GCP/Azure regions, not inside them. Host probes are experimental. Placement affects fetch handlers, not RPC/named entrypoints.

sources.title: Cloudflare Containers overview
claims: Available on Workers Paid; supports Linux runtime/library/filesystem needs; a Worker and Durable Object start/control each instance. Availability is documented; general availability/SLA is not established merely by absence of a beta banner.

sources.title: Container lifecycle and runtime
claims: Each linux/amd64 Container runs in a Firecracker microVM with its own kernel/network. Container and DO placement can differ. Requests enter via Worker/DO; start returns before readiness. Restart may move location.

sources.title: Container limits and instance types
claims: Predefined max4vCPU/12GiB/20GB. Custom minimum1vCPU and3GiB/vCPU, max4vCPU/12GiB/20GB. Account6TiB/1,500vCPU/30TB concurrent; image storage50GB. Snapshot20GB/30day refreshed-on-restore TTL.

sources.title: Container pricing
claims: 10ms billing; active CPU $0.000020/vCPU-s, provisioned RAM $0.0000025/GiB-s and disk $0.00000007/GB-s. Includes22,500vCPU-s/90,000GiB-s/720,000GB-s monthly. NA/EU egress$0.025/GB after1TB; Worker/DO charges additional.

sources.title: Container scheduling policies
claims: Default scheduler sets one application-wide image/size and uses provider rollouts/max_instances. durable_object policy is public beta, immutable policy choice, app-controlled image/size at start, no max_instances or provider image rollout.

sources.title: Container rollouts
claims: Worker activates before image/rollout and operations are not transactional. Deploy success only starts rollout. Old/new image compatibility needed. SIGTERM then up to15min before SIGKILL; default rollout grace0.

sources.title: Container placement
claims: Supports broad geographic-region and US/EU/fedramp jurisdiction constraints; not named cloud-zone co-location. Middle East/Oceania/Africa limited-capacity regions cannot be exclusively selected without support arrangement.

sources.title: Container outbound traffic
claims: Only HTTP80/HTTPS443 intercepted by outbound/host rules. With Internet enabled other ports bypass those rules; with it disabled other ports are denied. No documented tenant static TCP egress product established on this page.

sources.title: Container environment variables and secrets
claims: DO reads Worker secrets or bound store and passes selected values via start env. Running process keeps startup environment; updated values apply on next start.

sources.title: Container scaling and routing
claims: Unique IDs explicitly address separate instances; getting an ID alone does not start it. Documented use case is per-user backend. Random shared-instance routing is a different architecture.

sources.title: Durable Object Container API
claims: setInactivityTimeout controls time after DO inactivity and must reset after DO restart; getTcpPort returns fetch/connect access. Request cancellation does not automatically kill exec processes; DO fetch signal can be forwarded, RPC lacks it. Snapshot excludes memory/processes.

sources.title: Durable Objects pricing
claims: 1M requests and400,000GB-s included; $0.15/M requests and$12.50/M GB-s. Overage rounds to whole billable units. 128MB allocated billed/object; eligible hibernation not billed. DOs in same class can share isolate despite separate billed memory.

sources.title: Durable Objects limits
claims: Paid500 classes/account, unlimited objects; SQLite storage10GB/object. Single object single-threaded, soft1,000requests/s; Worker limits apply.

sources.title: D1 limits
claims: 50,000 paid databases/account; hard10GB/database,100 columns/table,30s query,2MB row/blob. D1 is provider-hosted SQLite state, not a remote-DB connector.

sources.title: R2 pricing
claims: Standard $0.015/GB-month,$4.50/M class A,$0.36/M class B; free10GB-month,1M A,10M B; Internet egressfree. Overages rounded to next units.

sources.title: Workers request AbortSignal
claims: enable_request_signal allows inbound request.signal abort listener on client disconnect. This is a documented hook, not proof of database cancellation through driver/pool/container chain.

sources.title: Container image management
claims: Default scheduler supports Cloudflare registry, Docker Hub, ECR, GAR; external registry images are not cached and can incur source egress. New DO scheduler requires Cloudflare registry digest-pinned images. Deleting old images can break rollback.

sources.title: Cloudflare Observability pricing effective December 1, 2026
claims: Current canonical table: from Dec1,2026 pooled account allowances50GB ingestion and10GB-month storage, thenUSD0.25/GB and0.10/GB-month. Workers/Containers logs and traces included. Ingestion is pre-compression incl enriched/custom attributes; storage=sum daily peak queryableGB/30. Seven-day default retention. Free/Pro/Business Workers Observability auto-migrate Dec1; Enterprise at renewal. Documentation inconsistency: worked example says(20-10)*0.10=0.80; this is wrong; use table and recompute. Search-cache version updatedOct2 showed12GB-month but canonical openedOct12 updatedOct5 shows10GB-month.

sources.title: Compute Plans
claims: 1c-2g is one CPU and 2 GB RAM for web/private/worker services.
August 2026 introduced specification-based plan IDs; existing legacy IDs remain accepted.
Each service replica is billed for its compute plan.

sources.title: Production-Grade Rails Hosting: Architecture & Scaling Guide
claims: Official article lists web-service 1c-2g at $25/month, 1 CPU and 2 GB RAM.
Web-service 0.5c-512mb is $7/month.
Do not confuse the web-service plan with separately priced Postgres plans.

sources.title: How much does cloud application hosting cost for small businesses
claims: Pro workspace is $25/month, with 25 GB outbound bandwidth and 1,000 pipeline minutes.
Hobby is $0/month, 5 GB bandwidth, 500 pipeline minutes and at most 25 services.
Scale workspace is $499/month with 1 TB bandwidth and 5,000 pipeline minutes.
Persistent disk is $0.25/GB/month.

sources.title: Platform Features by Plan
claims: Pro supports unlimited services, projects and environments.
Network-isolated environments, OIDC, dedicated outbound IP add-on and private links require Pro or higher.
Hobby service count includes suspended services.

sources.title: Service Types
claims: A service runs one or more containerized instances.
CPU and memory are determined by the service compute plan.
The page does not establish a tenant-dedicated guest kernel or physical host.

sources.title: Projects and Environments
claims: By default, all services within a workspace in the same region can communicate privately.
Environment network isolation blocks cross-environment private traffic but not public URLs or SSH.
Turning isolation on does not terminate existing connections; restart if required.
Deleting a project deletes its associated services and environments.

sources.title: Deploying an Image
claims: Prebuilt image must use linux/amd64 and be no larger than 10 GB compressed.
Immutable image digests can be specified.
Image-backed services do not automatically deploy after registry tag changes.
Render re-pulls images on some restarts, scaling and rollback; maintain old image availability.
ECR pull credentials expire after 12 hours; OIDC does not support image-backed ECR pulls.

sources.title: Health Checks
claims: HTTP health expects 2xx or 3xx within five seconds.
Unhealthy running instance stops receiving traffic after about 15 seconds and restarts after 60 seconds.
New deployment receives traffic after all new instances pass health checks.
A new deployment failing health for 15 minutes is cancelled while existing instances remain.

sources.title: Dedicated Outbound IPs
claims: A regional dedicated set comprises three IPv4 addresses; traffic may use any of them.
A set may apply to a workspace or selected environments.
Default workspace quota is four sets, increase by contacting support.

sources.title: Dedicated IPs for your services on Render
claims: May 19, 2026 announcement prices each dedicated regional IP set at $100/month.
Sets are an add-on available to Pro and higher workspaces.

sources.title: Private Links
claims: Private links are Pro+ and connect to supported resources hosted on AWS in the same region.
$30 per workspace per month covers up to three private links; higher needs require contact.
Public-provider and customer endpoint setup remains necessary.

sources.title: Render vs Vercel
claims: Render documents HTTP response duration up to 100 minutes.
Paid services are always on; free services can sleep.
The page documents WebSocket support.
Comparison claims about Vercel are not used as evidence about Vercel current limits.

sources.title: Persistent Disks
claims: Root filesystem is ephemeral unless a disk is attached.
A disk can attach to one service instance and prevents multi-instance scaling and zero-downtime deployments.
Automatic daily snapshots are retained at least seven days.
Disk snapshots should not replace database-native backups for transactional databases.

sources.title: OIDC on Render
claims: Pro+ provides automatically rotated short-lived per-service tokens.
Managed integrations document AWS, Anthropic and OpenAI.
AWS configuration supports one AWS_ROLE_ARN per service and AWS_WEB_IDENTITY_TOKEN_FILE.
IAM trust may match exact subject workspace:{WORKSPACE_ID}:environment:{ENVIRONMENT_ID}:service:{SERVICE_ID} and sts.amazonaws.com audience.
Docker builds and image-backed ECR pulls are not supported by this integration.

sources.title: Render-to-AWS OIDC authentication now generally available
claims: Render-to-AWS OIDC became generally available July 15, 2026 on Pro and higher.

sources.title: API Authentication
claims: Bearer API keys inherit access to all workspaces the owning user belongs to.
A per-service API key was not documented in this reference.

sources.title: Update service
claims: PATCH /v1/services/{serviceId} updates image and configuration.
An API update does not automatically trigger a deployment; explicitly trigger a deploy.
autoDeployTrigger replaces the deprecated autoDeploy field.

sources.title: Trigger deploy
claims: Trigger-deploy API accepts an imageUrl override with the same image host/repository/name.
201 means started and 202 means queued.
An override alone is not persistent desired-image configuration.

sources.title: Rollbacks
claims: API rollback does not disable auto-deploy.
Rollback restores target deployment settings but does not rewrite configured future state.
Disk contents, domains and compute plan do not roll back with the image.
Old images must remain available in the registry.

sources.title: API Rate Limiting
claims: Service creation is limited to 20/hour/user.
Service update/deploy/resume/suspend and deploy hooks are limited to 10/minute/service.
Custom-domain create/verify is limited to 50/hour/user.
Other POST/PATCH/DELETE requests are 30/minute, other GET requests 400/minute.
Read RateLimit headers; support can adjust limits.

sources.title: Custom Domains
claims: Pro includes 15 custom domains then charges $0.25/domain/month.
TLS certificates issue and renew automatically.
onrender.com hostname can be disabled after custom hostname readiness.
Render directs users to IPv4 configuration rather than AAAA records.

sources.title: Outbound Bandwidth
claims: Pro includes 25 GB per workspace, Hobby 5 GB, Scale 1 TB.
Public outbound excess is $0.15/GB and private-link outbound $0.03/GB.
Public HTTP/WebSocket responses and service-initiated public outbound count.
Same-region service-initiated traffic to Amazon S3 or Google Cloud Storage is exempt.
Inbound, same-region Render private traffic, and log/metrics streaming traffic are not billed as outbound.

sources.title: Pricing
claims: Current iad/ewr monthly examples: shared-2x/2 GB $13.39 and performance-1x/2 GB $33.
Stopped/suspended rootfs and provisioned volumes cost $0.15/GB/month.
US/EU internet egress is $0.02/GB; app-scoped static egress is $0.005/hour.
Dedicated ingress IPv4 is a separate $2/month.
Volume snapshots cost $0.08/GB/month after first 10 GB; no general platform subscription floor was identified.

sources.title: Security
claims: Fly states tenants do not share kernels and run in separate lightweight VMs.

sources.title: CPU Performance
claims: Shared vCPU baseline is five milliseconds per 80-millisecond period, 6.25%.
Shared Machines burst using credits; performance CPUs receive full CPU time.
Shared-2x is not two continuous dedicated physical cores.

sources.title: Custom Private Networks
claims: Default organization private network is shared.
Custom private network is selected during app creation and cannot be changed later.
Apps using the same custom network identity can communicate privately.

sources.title: Static Egress IPs
claims: App-scoped static egress survives Machine replacement and is regional.
Each IP supports up to 64 Machines and each Machine up to 1,024 connections per destination IP.
Both IPv4 and IPv6 allowlisting may be needed.

sources.title: Automatic Stop and Start
claims: Autostart wakes already-created Machines; it does not create new Machines.
Autostop evaluates every few minutes and stops one Machine per region per pass.
Minimum zero running Machines is configurable.

sources.title: Health Checks
claims: Health-check failure removes a Machine from routing but never automatically restarts or stops it.

sources.title: Machines API Resource
claims: API supports create, read, update, start, stop, suspend, delete, leases and version guards.
Updates submit full config rather than partial PATCH.
skip_launch=true allows updating a stopped Machine without starting it.
Region and name cannot change in place.

sources.title: Pricing
claims: Pro $20/month minimum counts toward resource usage.
RAM $10/GB-month; CPU $20/vCPU-month; public egress $0.05/GB; volume $0.15/GB-month.
Usage is metered rather than a fixed per-service monthly instance fee.

sources.title: Serverless
claims: Sleeping follows roughly five to ten minutes without outbound packets.
Database pools and telemetry can keep a service alive.
First request after sleep can receive 502; configuration changes apply after redeploy.

sources.title: Droplet Pricing
claims: Basic Regular 2 GiB/one shared vCPU/50 GiB disk/2,000 GiB transfer is $12/month.
Basic 1 GiB/one shared vCPU/25 GiB/1,000 GiB is $6/month.
Basic 8 GiB/four shared vCPU/160 GiB/5,000 GiB is $48/month.
CPU-Optimized two dedicated vCPU/4 GiB is $42/month.
January 1, 2026 introduced per-second billing, minimum 60 seconds or $0.01, capped at 672 hours/month.

sources.title: Droplet Pricing Details
claims: A Droplet is billed from creation to destruction, including when powered off.
Excess outbound costs $0.01/GiB; team allowances are pooled.
Inbound and private VPC traffic are free.

sources.title: Backups Pricing
claims: Weekly backups cost 20% of Droplet price; daily backups cost 30%.
Usage-priced alternatives charge retained restorable data and require separate modeling.

sources.title: Provide User Data
claims: Creation-time user-data/cloud-init can automate initial configuration.

sources.title: Metadata API
claims: Guest metadata at link-local 169.254.169.254 includes user-data.
Avoid putting long-lived provider control credentials in user-data.

sources.title: Droplet Policies
claims: Droplets are Linux VMs on virtualized hardware.
Droplets are completely unmanaged and support cannot directly access them.
The operator remains responsible for guest administration.

sources.title: Price Adjustment
claims: New orders and rescaling prices changed June 15, 2026; page updated July 8.
US Ashburn/Hillsboro CPX11 rises from $6.99 to $20.49/month excluding primary IPv4 and VAT.
US CPX21 rises from $13.99 to $37.49/month.
EU CX23 new $6.49 price is not a US price or evidence of US availability.

sources.title: Deploying on Render
claims: After healthy new-instance routing switch, Render waits 60 seconds then sends SIGTERM to the old instance.
Default graceful shutdown is 30 seconds, configurable up to 300 seconds, then SIGKILL.
100-minute HTTP duration is not a guarantee a stream survives a deploy.

sources.title: Automated Security Response on AWS: Cost
claims: Current official US East/N. Virginia example S3 row: first 50 TB storage $0.023 per GB-month.
S3 PUT/COPY/POST/LIST $0.005 per 1000; GET/other $0.0004 per 1000.
Only the S3 rate row is used; other service estimates are outside this research.

sources.title: S3 Pricing
claims: S3 storage GB are binary units of 2^30 bytes.
First 100 GB monthly internet outbound is shared across AWS services and regions except China/GovCloud.
S3-to-AWS-service transfers within the same AWS region are exempt.
Render region labels alone do not prove the underlying AWS region or route.

sources.title: IAM FAQs
claims: IAM itself is offered at no additional charge.
Some optional IAM Access Analyzer capabilities are separately paid.

sources.title: Using SSE-S3
claims: New S3 objects are encrypted by default with SSE-S3.
SSE-S3 adds no extra encryption charge; configuration API calls have normal request pricing.
Object metadata is not encrypted by server-side encryption.

sources.title: Retaining multiple versions with S3 Versioning
claims: Versioning preserves multiple object versions; all retained versions must be included in storage estimates.

PostgreSQL client connection settings and timeouts
